.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

- 2) Forecast remains uncertain as a coastal low tracks up the 
  Eastern Seaboard Sunday into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and warm conditions expected to continue 
through Saturday.

Surface high pressure remains overhead through Friday. This will
continue to bring very dry conditions and calm winds. Highs will
be above average with temperatures in the 60s to even the low 70s
through Friday. Clear skies and light winds overnight yield favorable
conditions for radiational cooling. Overnight lows will drop into
the 30s tonight with lows Thursday and Friday night staying in 
the mid 30s to 40s. 

While remaining overhead, surface high pressure begins shifting
northward on Saturday as a low pressure system develops off the
coast of Florida and tracks north. This results in increased
cloud cover although dry conditions and calm winds persist.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Forecast remains uncertain as a coastal low tracks 
up the Eastern Seaboard Sunday into Monday. 

An area of low pressure is forecast to develop off the Southeast 
U.S. coast late this week, then track northward along the coast this 
weekend. The low's initial forward speed is going to be slow as it 
gets trapped underneath a brief, weak upper ridge, then quickly 
picks up speed as it moves northeast with a strong upper trough 
approaching from the OH Valley. There remains considerable 
differences among the global guidance, both run to run and between 
models in each run. The ensemble guidance for both the European and 
GFS remain quite dispersive with low tracks well inland across the 
NC/VA Piedmont to well offshore of the Mid-Atlantic. Of particular 
interest are the Euro and GFS AI models that are more in line with 
each other, both indicating a low track between I-95 and the 
coastline. The low pressure quickly deepens and rapidly tracks 
toward southern New England and Nova Scotia Monday into Monday 
night. 

At this time there remains too much uncertainty to pin down any 
specific details or impacts to our area. Rain chances Sunday into 
Sunday night have steadily increased, especially east of the Blue 
Ridge with the highest certainty east of I-95. The exact track of 
the low is going to be critical to where the heaviest rain falls, 
though there could be a sharp gradient on the western side of the 
precip shield from heavy to very light rain amounts. It is worth 
mentioning the higher-end of the ensemble spread indicates 2-4" as a 
worst-case scenario, but many members also have little to no rain 
for most of the area - this probably speak the best to how much 
uncertainty remains. The location of the heaviest QPF also varies 
greatly from along US-15 to the Delmarva. Continue to monitor the 
forecast over the next few days as guidance hopefully starts to 
converge on a solution for this weekend. 

A strong Canadian High builds across much of the central to eastern 
CONUS during the early part of next week. This is going to bring us 
dry, brisk, and much colder conditions. 

Models are indicating the potential for another system near 
Thanksgiving, but even more spread exists with that system. 
More updates as we get closer.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Light winds out of the south to southwest are expected today 
with winds becoming light and variable overnight. On Friday, 
winds shift to northwesterly before shifting to southeasterly on
Saturday. 

We continue to monitor the developing coastal low off the coast
of Florida. As this low pressure system drifts northward, 
precipitation and sub-VFR conditions are possible by Sunday and
continuing into Monday across the terminals. The greatest 
chance will be for the eastern terminals, but there is still a
lot of uncertainty with potential storm track at this time.

&&

.MARINE...
High pressure will remain over the area throughout the entire week.
The lighter winds support favorable conditions across the marine
waters. A low pressure system is forecast to develop off the coast
of Florida and may bring precipitation and increased winds to the
waters on Sunday which may approach SCA criteria. SCAs likely by
late Sunday night through Monday as the low pressure system rides
up the east coast. Stronger winds will be possible, but will depend
on the exact track of the low. Should the low trend closer to the
coast, Gale-force winds can't be ruled out Monday.
